ai.title: Move analytics init before agent registry in CLI
ai.summary: Relocates `initAnalytics()` and `trackEvent(AnalyticsEvent.APP_LAUNCHED)` to run before agent registry initialization in `cli/src/index.tsx`. Prevents `trackEvent` throws from logger calls occurring during registry load. Internal timing fix in CLI startup sequence.

eli5.text: When you launch the tool from the command line, it now starts up its usage tracking before it loads your custom agents, so that logging messages from the agent-loading step no longer cause errors. The startup sequence was rearranged internally, and you as a user won't see anything different except that rare startup crashes caused by that logging error are less likely to occur. This is already live in the current version.

ai.title: CLI version bumped to 1.0.621
ai.summary: The Freebuff CLI package version advanced to 1.0.621 in cli/release/package.json. This release aggregates prior same-day work, including the deterministic write_file constraint that now requires complete file content (removing edit snippet support), the analytics-init relocation before agent registry load in cli/src/index.tsx, and new subscriber profitability analysis tooling. Documentation corrections to quick-start, troubleshooting, modes, and model tables also ship in this bump.
ai.evidence: cli/release/package.json version string changed from 1.0.620 to 1.0.621 (single-line hunk on the "version" field).

eli5.text: This release makes the Freebucks coding assistant more reliable and easier to understand. The agent now requires you to write out complete file content instead of using shortcuts or placeholders, which prevents confusion when saving code changes. New internal tools were added to analyze subscription profitability, and the analytics system now starts up before the agent registry so event tracking is more stable. Documentation was cleaned up across the quick-start, troubleshooting, and model comparison guides so installation help and cache-clearing steps are clearer. Upgrading gives you steadier startup performance, more accurate file saving, and easier-to-follow guides when you run into issues. Overall, Freebucks is now smoother to launch, safer to use, and simpler to troubleshoot.
